purpose: Teach: スナップ/ソックス/メッシュ/１番/合コン/酔っ払っ/愛嬌/おしっこ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがスナップ写真を毎日撮られた
lines.en: When he was young, your father used to take snapshots every single day.
lines.style: Soft opening, as if retrieving a memory from decades back. Quiet, steady pace. Voice settles gently on the image of the father. Slightly wistful but grounded—not performative.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、ウールソックスを毎冬編まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and you—your mother knitted you wool socks every winter, didn't she, dear?
lines.style: Warm affirmation, then a gentle redirect. Playful lilt on the memory of the socks. The 'didn't she, dear?' is tender and teasing at once—inviting him to sit with his own history.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがメッシュの帽子を愛用された
lines.en: When he was young, your father favoured that mesh cap. Wore it constantly.
lines.style: Quieter still. Gaze turned inward on the specific image—the cap itself. Breath held slightly on 'constantly.' Not dwelling, but lingering just long enough to let it matter.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、職場で１番の働き者と呼ばれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And at work they called you the hardest worker there, didn't they, dear?
lines.style: Bright acknowledgment, but not exaggerated. The praise lands matter-of-factly, as if stating something she's always known. 'Didn't they, dear?' carries the warmth of someone watching him accept a compliment he doesn't quite believe.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは合コンに興味を持たれなかった
lines.en: When he was young, your father had no interest in those group dates people were always arranging.
lines.style: Slight smile in the voice, knowing what's coming. Speaks as if this is a gentle secret between them. The admission is fond, not critical—the tone of someone saying, 'I knew who you were even then.'

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お酒で酔っ払った事は一度も無かったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You never got drunk a single time, did you, dear? Not once.
lines.style: Admiration wrapped in tenderness. The repetition of 'not once' is quiet but emphatic—she's proud of this, and she wants him to feel her seeing it. Slight emphasis on 'you' at the start.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは愛嬌のあるお客様を大事にされた
lines.en: When he was young, your father made sure to look after the customers who had charm, the ones worth remembering.
lines.style: Thoughtful, slightly amused. The word 'charm' carries a note of recognition—she understands what he valued, what he saw in people. Voice settles, as if this explains something about him that mattered.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫のおしっこの世話まで下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you—you even helped change your grandchildren's nappies without being asked, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm, slightly mischievous. The intimacy of this memory—the small, unglamorous acts of care—delivered with genuine delight. Soft peak on 'didn't you,' then settling into affection. Breath easy and close.
